newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechen rebel hero turns 32 in confident mood.
newsitem.headline: Chechen rebel hero turns 32 in confident mood.

text.p: He may be one of Russia's most wanted men, but in breakaway Chechnya Shamil Basayev is revered as a hero and on Tuesday his compatriots had a chance to show their appreciation for the man who defied Moscow.

About 100 guests gathered at a restaurant -- one of the few in the Chechen capital Grozny to survive nearly two years of fighting -- to mark Basayev's 32nd birthday and wish him success in this month's presidential election.
The bearded Basayev, one of Chechnya's boldest and most fiery rebel fighters, is a front-runner in the race for the tiny mountainous region's presidency on January 27.
"I shall win this election straight off, there will be no second round," Basayev said with a broad smile.
The election is a first crucial step in restoring order in Chechnya following last August's peace accord with Moscow that halted 21 months of fighting between the separatists and Russian troops.

Under the deal, Chechnya's final political status has been deferred for five years. But all the Chechen presidential candidates, including Basayev, believe that is a face-saving formula following Moscow's military defeat and withdrawal.
They all insist Chechnya is already a fully independent state, though Moscow still hopes to persuade the region to remain within the Russian Federation.
Basayev is the candidate Moscow would least like to win the presidency. He became public enemy number one after leading a spectacular raid on the southern Russian town of Budennovsk in June 1995.
A group of Chechen rebels under his command seized hostages in a hospital and more than 100 people were killed.
Basayev became a hero in rebel ranks after negotiating directly by telephone with Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and escaping unpunished with his fellow fighters.
The outcome was seen as a humiliation for the Kremlin.

On Tuesday Basayev, who has been campaigning for the election in his trademark army fatigues and cap, wore a suit, brightly coloured tie and traditional Chechen lambswool hat for the first time since the start of the war in December 1994.
His guests wore medals bearing the symbol of Chechen independence -- a black wolf against a green background.
The party began after dusk, in accordance with Islamic tradition during the period of Ramadan.

Some of Chechnya's most popular singers and poets performed for Basayev and his guests, who included two other presidential candidates -- former information minister Movladi Udugov and former culture minister Ahmed Zakayev.
Among the many gifts Basayev received were a dagger and a traditional Caucasian sabre. Udugov gave Basayev a Chechen flag "sewn by special order with special cloth".

Basayev's two other main rivals for the presidency, acting president Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev and the former head of government Aslan Maskhadov, did not attend the party, though seats had been prepared for them.
The pragmatic Maskhadov is Moscow's preferred candidate for the post of president.
